content.introduction: Big Tech earnings this week are expected to drive market momentum, with strong results likely to boost global indices and investor confidence. Analysts predict significant growth, setting a positive tone for the rest of the earnings season. The Magnificent Seven's performance will be crucial for market direction.
body: Coming off another all-time closing high for the S&P 500 last Friday, it is the busiest week of first-quarter earnings season, with 180 S&P 500 companies scheduled to report. Companies reporting and combining actual results with consensus estimates for companies yet to report, the S&P 500’s blended earnings growth rate for the quarter is 15.1% year over year, above the 13.2% expectations at the end of the quarter. Because technology companies are critical drivers of earnings growth and account for a significant percentage of the S&P 500’s market capitalization, the Magnificent 7 remains the group to watch this earnings season. Beyond earnings, the status of hostilities with Iran and oil prices are likely to remain a focus for financial markets this week. Interestingly, the financial markets continue to price in a low probability of an economic or earnings downturn despite the decline in the odds of the end of the conflict with Iran in the betting markets.

Big Tech is about to remind investors who really drives global markets. This week, Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL), Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN), Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOGL), Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT) and Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META) will report their third-quarter results, and my expectation is that these earnings will come in ahead of forecasts, igniting a rally that carries through the end of the year. Futures linked to the Nasdaq and S&P 500 rose ahead of the announcements, showing that investors are positioning for stronger profits from the world’s largest technology firms. If Big Tech earnings and a Fed rate cut occur together, Bitcoin and other alternative assets could continue to advance as investors diversify their holdings. The Magnificent Seven already account for more than half of the S&P 500’s gains this year, and their influence is likely to expand further. My prediction is that Big Tech will exceed expectations this week, extend gains into year-end, and help drive global indices to new highs by the end of 2025.

Big technology earnings this week could offer a much-needed catalyst for a market under pressure. For the better part of the year, technology stocks have propelled the stock market higher as investors ramped up bets on the growth prospects of artificial intelligence. Big Tech's performance this week could set the tone for the rest of earnings season and revive the market momentum. Longtime Deutsche Bank Tesla bull Emmanuel Rosner also downgraded the stock to hold from a buy rating as Tesla looks poised to pivot from building its low-cost entry vehicle to focusing on self-driving technology.
